paper.title: In Prospect and Retrospect: Reflective Memory Management for Long-term Personalized Dialogue Agents
paper.central_claim: Reflective Memory Management (RMM): Prospective Reflection (topic-based summarization into a memory bank with LLM add/merge) plus Retrospective Reflection (online REINFORCE update of a lightweight reranker from LLM citation rewards) improves long-term personalized dialogue, e.g. >5% over the strongest baseline on MSC and LongMemEval.

gap.author_gap: Rigid memory granularity fragments semantic structure; fixed retrievers cannot adapt to domains/users; labeled data for personalized retrievers is expensive.
gap.checked_gap: Both limits are concretely tested: granularity comparison shows fixed units underperform an adaptive-granularity oracle (E009), and direct retriever RL fails without a reranker (E005); but neighbors beyond MemoryBank/LD-Agent are only cited.
lineage: MemoryBank (forgetting-curve memory) / LD-Agent (long/short banks, keyword retrieval) / Theanine (timeline retrieval) -> RMM (topic memory + citation-driven reranker)
gap.closest_adjacent: MemoryBank and LD-Agent (run as baselines per the paper); Theanine, MemGPT, Mem0, A-Mem are named in Related Work but not compared; original texts not in pinned input package
gap.residue: Fragmented topics across turns/sessions; retriever mismatch with how the generator uses evidence.
gap.stakes: RAG Acc 58.8 vs RMM 61.2 (Contriever); Recall@5 54.3 vs 60.4.
gap.method_response: Topic-level summarization with merge; online reranker adapting to generator citations.
gap.remaining_gap: Scaling of memory (no forgetting/pruning), multi-modal, cost, privacy; no comparison with newer memory managers.
